verdict_rationale: Path relocation to .prflow/tmp/create-issue/<slug>/ is thorough and internally consistent across skills/create-issue/**, scripts/issue-audit-state.py, prompt extension, and docs. The new reaper scripts/cleanup-create-issue-run.sh is slug-keyed, fail-closed, traversal-safe, best-effort, and has strong behavioral test coverage. All six acceptance criteria are satisfied. The only cross-cutting finding is a stale documentation coupled-mirror (docs/internal/cloud-allowlist.md still names the old flat issue-body path); it is human-read, tool-consumed by nothing, the illustrative point still holds for the new path, and it breaks no behavior or AC. Non-blocking. Remaining findings are test-hardening and comment-accuracy suggestions.

phase3_findings.description: Unreconciled coupled-mirror: docs/internal/cloud-allowlist.md:1018 and :1038 still document the OLD flat redirect target `<main-root>/.prflow/tmp/issue-body-<slug>.md` for create-issue/references/issue-template.md, but issue-template.md:197 now composes `<main-root>/.prflow/tmp/create-issue/<slug>/issue-body-<slug>.md`. CLAUDE.md coupled-invariant discipline requires documenting sites of a relocated literal to be reconciled in the same change. Non-blocking: human-read adjudication doc, no tool consumes it, and the illustrative point (a <main-root>/-prefixed redirect containing .prflow/tmp evades the anchored matcher pattern) still holds for the new path.

Pointer-removal branch (cleanup-create-issue-run.sh:53-63) executes independently of the dir-removal guard, but every test seeding a pointer also seeds the run dir. No test covers 'own-slug pointer present, run dir absent -> pointer still removed', so a future refactor nesting pointer cleanup inside the dir-exists guard would pass the suite while orphaning the shared pointer.

AC6 (pre-existing flat issue-* files survive) has no direct regression pin. The reaper is structurally safe today (only touches create-issue/<slug>/ and the namespaced pointer), but a one-line test seeding a sibling flat file and asserting survival would pin the invariant a future scope-broadening could violate.

Slug-safety comment (cleanup-create-issue-run.sh:27-29) attributes both the empty-slug and the path-unsafe-slug hazard to 'collapse to the shared namespace root', but that rationale is accurate only for the empty slug; a traversal/absolute slug would instead escape the namespace and rm -rf a path outside it (the more dangerous case the regex guard actually prevents). Split the rationale.

rm -rf failure arm prints 'warning: could not remove' to stderr but the script always exit 0s and also prints on success, so the only failure signal is the literal 'warning:' token in stderr; no machine-readable channel. Acceptable for a best-effort reaper an LLM agent reads, noted only for a future non-agent caller.

per_reviewer_assessment.prflow:silent-failure-hunter: No defects; one Suggestion (exit-0 masks rm failure). Verified nested dir created before every writer via mkdir(parents=True); refusal arms exit before deletion; pointer read non-destructive.
per_reviewer_assessment.prflow:comment-analyzer: One Suggestion (imprecise slug-safety comment). All issue-audit-state.py docstrings and test comments accurately updated to the new path; no stale old-path comment survives.
per_reviewer_assessment.prflow:pr-test-analyzer: Coverage strong; two hardening Suggestions (pointer-without-dir case; AC6 direct pin). 11 behavioral reaper cases; state.py nested path exercised end-to-end; AC5 pinned at rendered surface.
per_reviewer_assessment.prflow:requesting-code-review: Verdict ready-to-merge. All 6 ACs satisfied with concrete evidence; reaper fail-closed and slug-safe; mkdir-before-write confirmed on every writer. Same cloud-allowlist mirror flagged as non-blocking Minor.
